findings.title: Owner row 30 presents the AUD-2 arming-chain exemption as load-bearing, but the project's own GND-via spot search finds a legal spot 0.671 mm from 3 of its 4 vias

evidence.measured: Probe copy of tools/ with BAT_ENABLE / BAT_SW_SOURCE / BAT_SW_RETURN removed from R10_SLOW_RETURN_NETS (all else unchanged): route_check --profile r10 fails exactly 4 critical_via_no_gnd: BAT_SW_SOURCE (10.8,69.2) 7.467 mm, BAT_ENABLE (21.3,68.9) 1.866 mm, (19.675,66.6) 1.875 mm, (17.1,82.8) 2.902 mm (row 30's figures reproduce). r7_hygiene.gnd_spots(board, via, GND_REACH, first=True), the search M2 says decides whether a missing-GND-via entry still holds, returns a legal 0.5 mm GND via at (10.2,68.9), (20.7,69.2) and (20.275,66.3), each 0.671 mm away; none for (17.1,82.8). S-8 does not count GND at BAT_ENABLE / BAT_SW_RETURN barrels (check_r10 BARREL_GND_HAZARD = ACT_GATE, ACT_DRV, PYRO1_OUT): GND there holds U9 off.
evidence.physics: BAT_SW_SOURCE and BAT_SW_RETURN sit behind 470 kOhm each (R80, R165), BAT_ENABLE is (R80+R165)||R81 x C87 = 227 kOhm x 220 nF = 50 ms; currents are about 7 uA. A return partner via does nothing for such a node, so the exemption is physically rooted (agrees with D-R21-04).

findings.impact: The owner is asked to accept row 30 on the premise that the rule cannot be met; M2 asks for any exception's reason to be re-measured, and an allowlist entry for three of these vias would be stale. The real reason is physics (no fast edge), not impossibility. No electrical impact.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only: in row 30 (and D-R21-04) state that the project's spot search finds legal GND spots 0.671 mm from three of the vias and none for (17.1,82.8), and that the exemption rests on the 50 ms / 7 uA physics, not on lack of room. Alternatively (board change, not recommended for the closing pair) add the three GND vias and leave only (17.1,82.8) exempt.

findings.title: K-rules pins only four rows of JLC's hole table; PTH annular ring and the 0.50 mm non-plated hole minimum are held by nothing (seeded)

evidence.jlc: https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities (read 2026-10-31): PTH annular ring >= 0.20 mm, multilayer 1 oz absolute minimum 0.15 mm; Min. non-plated holes 0.50 mm; via diameter 0.1 mm larger than hole; via to via 0.2 mm; NPTH to track 0.2 mm; inner via 0.2 / PTH 0.3 mm; PTH to track 0.28 (0.35 recommended); solder mask bridge 0.10 mm; silkscreen 0.15 / 1.0 mm.
evidence.seeded: Probe copy of the board: J122.5 drill 1.3 -> 1.7 mm (ring 0.30 -> 0.10 mm) and one J2 NPTH 0.991 -> 0.40 mm. kicad-cli 10.0.7 DRC (all severities) reports only one hole_clearance on J122.5 (inner 0.55 rule); no annular-ring or hole-size violation. check_r10 contains no annular / NPTH-size test (grep). min_through_hole_diameter 0.3 and min_via_annular_width 0.1 (vias only) are the only related floors.
evidence.board_now: Measured on 5516eeec: PTH rings 0.30 (DB125, 1.3/1.9 mm) and 0.20 (J3 slots); NPTH 0.60 (J3) and 0.991 (J2); vias 295 x 0.5/0.3, 4 x 0.6/0.3, 1 x 1.0/0.5; least via hole to via hole 0.259 mm; least via hole to PTH hole 0.681 mm; PTH hole to foreign copper >= 0.551 mm on all four layers; J3 NPTH to J3 GND SMD lands 0.200 mm (JLC NPTH-to-track 0.2, at the limit, maker land); least mask web 0.150 mm (U4); least track 0.2 mm.

findings.impact: M2's 'design rules within JLC's limits' is met by the board as built (every JLC row checked holds), but two hole-table rows are not gated, so a re-pinned footprint could break them silently. Footprints are SHA-pinned by K-lands, which limits but does not remove the gap.
findings.concrete_fix: Checks only: add to JLC_HOLE_TABLE (or a board measurement beside pth_inner_copper) every PTH pad ring >= 0.15 mm (fail) / 0.20 mm (recommended) and every NPTH drill >= 0.50 mm; optionally DRU rules '(condition "A.Type == 'Pad' && A.Pad_Type == 'NPTH, mechanical'") (constraint hole_size (min 0.5mm))'. Name the J3 NPTH-to-land 0.200 mm as an at-limit maker-land figure in M2 / ORDERING.

findings.title: No requirement or bench item covers ESD on J400, the operator-touched arming switch

evidence.measured: J400.1 BAT_SW_SOURCE -> R80 470 kOhm -> BAT_IN (D8 SMBJ12CA there); J400.2 BAT_SW_RETURN -> R165 470 kOhm -> BAT_ENABLE (U9.1 EN, R81 300 kOhm, C87 220 nF at U9's end since D-R21-05). No clamp on J400 (the GPS / radio / AUX / camera ports have ESD diodes). grep of REQUIREMENTS / ORDERING / FMEA / R10_VALIDATION for ESD together with J400 / screw switch: no hit.
evidence.calculation: Inference: an IEC 61000-4-2 style 150 pF / 8 kV contact that fully transfers into C87 gives 1.2 uC / 220 nF = 5.5 V on top of EN's 2.03 V maximum divider level, about 7.5 V against TPS25947 EN/UVLO absolute maximum 6.5 V (TI SLVSFC9C section 6.1 p7). On a floating vehicle the transfer is limited by the vehicle's capacitance to earth, so the real figure is likely far smaller; R165 flash-over is not characterised.

findings.impact: The single external screw switch (owner decision 2026-10-28) is turned by hand on the rail; a screw switch whose screw is a contact puts the operator's discharge straight onto J400. The worst credible result is EN overstress / U9 damage (board off or latched, fail safe for firing), not a fire path. Unqualified, not demonstrated.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only: add J400 ESD to F8 / F9's qualification list and ORDERING 8.3 (touch airframe / pad ground before the switch; first article: contact discharge at the switch screw in flight configuration, then the switch-off and J121.2 checks). A board change (a clamp at J400.2) is a respin option only.

findings.concrete_fix: Text only: add C88 (and 'Q120's drain') to the OQ-6 bullet in REQUIREMENTS Accepted risks; change ORDERING's U4 row citation to 2026-10-31T23:23Z.
